context.body: The family relationship is established before the burning bush and the return journey.
context.label: Narrative or literary frame

observations.body: Moses remains with Jethro, receives Zipporah as his wife, and names their son Gershom.
observations.label: Zipporah and Gershom enter Moses’ story: action

observations.body: The name remembers Moses’ life as a foreigner in a foreign land.
observations.label: Zipporah and Gershom enter Moses’ story: response

payload.posture: Read Exodus 2:21–22 as family already named evidence before carrying it into another source.
payload.tension: The later crisis calls the child “her son” without naming him, so Exodus 2 supplies family context but not a complete identification of every referent.
payload.title: Zipporah and Gershom enter Moses’ story
